dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: ...Ah, and just like that, she's left... She looked like she was in pain, too. Must've had to go take her medicine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what's it about this time?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: #Oh, just in time, {NICKNAME}! Remember that case from before? I already cracked it.

choices.text: Elementary for dear Heizou, I see!

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: I suppose I can tell you the whole story. You look like you might explode from curiosity otherwise... She probably won't come after me for leaking the case details.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: In short, the culprit was a student who frequented second-hand bookshops. Too poor to buy books, he'd just read them on-site.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: One day, he wrote a letter confessing his love to the girl he admired in secret and planned to slip it into her desk.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: But in the end, shyness got the better of him, and he retrieved it unopened.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Dejected, he began to head back home. And on the way, he wanted to crumple the letter into a ball and toss it, but couldn't bear to do that either, so he began mindlessly fanning himself with it...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Just then, he passed by a second-hand bookshop. So, to distract himself from his problems, he decided to head in and finish the novel he'd started reading a few days earlier.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: After finishing "The Flesh-Eating Tree That You Shouldn't Mess With!", he returned home... only to discover that his love letter was nowhere to be seen.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Exactly. He had accidentally used his love letter as a bookmark while reading.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: By the time he realized his mistake and returned to retrieve it, he found... that the book had already been sold, and the shopkeeper couldn't recall the buyer's name.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If anyone saw that letter...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: The poor kid must've been driving himself crazy, thinking, "If anyone reads that, I'm done for! I've got to get it back, no matter what!"

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Desperate, he turned to the modus operandi he'd read about in that same crime novel to retrieve it.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: I don't know if it's because he's actually really talented, due to the book's meticulous and detailed descriptions, or maybe because Inazuma City's been so safe lately that nobody bothers with basic precautions...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: But he succeeded. He used the criminal techniques in the book to conduct numerous break-ins and threw all of Hanamizaka into chaos.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: As the case was initially pretty minor, only the Doushin were assigned to the case at first. But as investigations stalled out, the public got more and more restless.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: So, Madam Kujou Sara assigned me to take charge. Fortunately, it wasn't too complicated, and as for the process... Well, I'd say things went pretty smoothly.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, how'd you catch the guy?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: *cough*... Well, I didn't really catch him, per se. One of the Doushin from the station bought a copy of "The Flesh-Eating Tree That You Shouldn't Mess With!".

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: He was going on about how "I gotta see for myself how good a book that can make a criminal willing to risk it all is."

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: And when he opened it, the letter just... fell out. After reading this "baffling" love letter, everything clicked.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: So, I just picked a time when classes were about to finish, intercepting our little "criminal" on his way out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He didn't even try to run?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Of course he did! Turned tail and was about to bolt the second he saw me. So I just said:

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: "If you run, I'll show the letter to your crush's deskmate."

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: No sooner had I finished speaking than he meekly surrendered.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: It was a bluff! I'd never actually follow through with something that low.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: He might be a kid, but a crime is a crime, and crimes come with consequences. He'll have to take responsibility and pay all the restitution required.

choices.text: He was a bit too good at it...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: *sigh*... That's why I say that crime novels that romanticize crime end up desensitizing people to it.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: "Something like this isn't really illegal, right?" "No harm, no foul!" "It's no big deal..."

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Once ideas like that start worming into people's minds, they might unknowingly turn into fools who cross the line.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! Do you think like that?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Hahaha! Really? It's okay if you do. It's only a crime if you act on such thoughts, after all.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Oh! Would you look at the time? I should head back to the station. The pile of cases on my desk isn't going to solve itself.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: After a debacle like this, I'm sure it won't be long before Madam Kujou takes us all on another public safety lecture tour...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: *sigh* Let's just hope we don't have any idiot copycat criminals. Otherwise... overtime beckons... again...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Oh my! Really? Tread lightly, then. Should you act on these thoughts, I might get put on your trail, and next thing you know, Madam Kujou will be clapping you in irons.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: And we'd best avoid that scenario. She's rough with the cuffs, to say nothing of the chafing when she leads you around.

choices.text: Feels like he's got a very dangerous talent...
Don't detectives walk the path of righteousness?
Leave the letter stuck inside the book... did he?
Was there but one truth this time?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Naturally! Madam Kujou Sara wouldn't approve of closing a case if there was any doubt.
